name: Copy trading with forensic and statistical wallet screening
one_line: Mirror a few slow-conviction wallets that pass a sign-randomisation null and an out-of-sample re-test, detected on-chain in ~2 s (the Data API feeds batch and stall for minutes), copying taker entries only; uplift is small and abstract-only, follower evidence is self-reported, and the copy-bot market has shrunk 88% since April.
maturity: Emerging and shrinking; skilled-minority premise is hard data (3.14% skilled, 44% persist), the +1.62 pp return to imitation is abstract-only, follower PnL evidence is three self-reported accounts, copy-bot volume down 88% Apr-Sep 2026
requires_ai: no; statistics select leaders, LLM optional only to read an unfamiliar market's rules
edge: Free-riding a small persistent skilled minority on a public tape before the price moves
capital: $1k-$10k; capacity-bound by leaders' taker ticket sizes and thin books
build_time: 4-6 weeks solo from scratch; 1-2 weeks of screening work on an existing copier
opportunity_size: Copy-bot flow $125M (Apr) to $15M (Sep MTD); +1.62 pp per market on ~$20k/month turnover is ~$320; shrinking
expected_results: Self-reported: +$257 on $500, +$171 on $10k paper, -8% on $150; guess -5% to +4%/month
competition: 43 copy bots, 5 vendors at 0.5-1% per fill; no audited follower PnL
flag: none for copying public fills; grey for selling auto-execution or leader coordination
validate: Walk-forward on vgregoire/polymarket-users at +10 s fill; beat top-50 PnL baseline by 1 pp/market; then 30-day shadow
top_risk: Leaders are makers, one-shots or bait; API feeds stall minutes; fees and repricing exceed the 1.6 pp budget
solo_fit_reason: Cheap to run and the owner already has the copier, but the measurable return is a few hundred dollars a month at $10k, half the screened leaders are noise by construction, the best leaders are uncopyable makers or high-frequency small tickets, and the product category is collapsing; worth keeping as a screening pipeline that feeds files 27 and 81 rather than as a standalone earner.
speed_class: execution-sensitive: copyable leaders reprice cents either way within minutes; detection must be on-chain (~2 s) because both Data API feeds batch-stall for minutes; latency leaders are dead at 1 s
results_1k: barely; -$90 to +$40/month (guess), fixed RPC/VPS cost dominates
min_capital: ~$5k; $20-60 fixed cost and one 5c tail erase a $1k book
capacity_ceiling: ~$25-50k solo; leaders' taker fills $250-2,500 median, books move 3-8c under size
services: Polymarket Data API v2 (/v2/trades, /v2/user-stats; reconciliation, not detection)
Jon Becker parquet / poly_data HyperSync backfill
changes_made: Written 2026-09-28 with live checks: v1/v2 leaderboards (top-50 overlaps), six leader tapes in taker-only and all-fills modes with maker shares, full closed-position ledgers and sign-randomisation nulls for Theo4 and Fredi9999, an on-chain OrderFilled to Data API ingestion-lag experiment (45/45 fills seen in /v2/trades at median 6.4 s; v1 /trades lagged 35-395 s), follower slippage on the leaders' 25 most recent fills against live books (median 1.0-1.2c), builder volumes for the copy bots Oct 2025 to Sep 2026, the public PolyCop builder-trades feed, and /v2/user-stats for e46m3 and RN1.

Maturity kept at Emerging but re-framed as shrinking, per the critic note: the file leads with the +1.62 pp abstract, the three self-reported follower results and the 88% collapse in copy-bot volume rather than with the build.
Critic note on 'selling into copy-followers' and thin-book front-running: placed as a hazard paragraph (underestimating point 8) with the trade itself referred to file 27.

Corrected the pack's copy-bot fee anchor to a live per-fill example (PolyCop builderFee 0.5% of sizeUsdc) and recorded that /trades rows carry no builder field (v1 or v2 schema); builder attribution is on-chain or via /builder/trades only.

Recorded Data API v1 endpoint semantics found live: /closed-positions is sorted by realizedPnl descending with 50 rows per page; /trades?user= does not default a side; /v2/user-stats exposes maker_rebate, taker_rebate, fees_refunded.
V1 exchange address in the writer brief (0x4bFb…982E) replaced by the V2 exchanges from E1 (0xE111…996B, 0xe222…0F59) after the cutover of 2026-04-28.

Cite-check + skeptic pass 2026-09-28 (26 numbered sources re-fetched or re-queried, 3 pack refs re-read; SSRN full text of [2] still unreachable via curl, WebFetch, arXiv and a web search): HN attribution fixed (the 'why is copy-trading popular' question is swingboy's, not SamPatt's); [9]'s own counterfactual added (skipped entries would have made +$1,485, filter unproven, Welch t = 0.69) and its repo date corrected; [3] dated to the arXiv listing (published 05-04, v2 05-14; body says Aug 24) and attributed to Gómez-Cram, Guo, Jensen and Kung; [10] 'hidden accounts' replaced by the interview's 'activity across wallets' and the top-ten category mix added; [11] corrected: the changelog's 09-04 entry itself documents 150 ms; [1] URL trimmed to the one relevant submission; [S1] replaced by the fetched Polygun review page [27], MEXC dropped; Theo4/Fredi9999 ledgers restated as 22/66 closed positions in 14/45 markets and 9/30 events with re-run p-values (0.0055 / 0.0199); Papeasy's tapes do not overlap and its last fill is 2026-08-14 (September PnL is marked); live re-runs of leaderboards, six leader tapes, user-stats, builder volumes and PolyCop builder trades reproduced within drift. Material change: a second latency window (21:07-21:15 UTC) showed the Data API v2 feed stalling: newest row 105-195 s old, 0 of 77 on-chain fills seen in 90 s, one refresh in five minutes, per-user queries for RN1 frozen 297-353 s, v1 495-545 s; detection is now stated as on-chain only, the v2 feed as a reconciliation source. Follower-slippage re-run on the then-latest 25 fills gave medians of -2.0c (RN1) and 0c (e46m3) with tails -14c to +12c, so the drift claim is restated as two-sided repricing of mostly maker rows rather than follower slippage. Added that no v1/v2 row carries a maker/taker field and that on-chain OrderFilled pairs (maker record naming the taker; taker record naming the exchange) are the only sub-block-time way to tell which side the leader was on.
open_doubts: Oliphant's +1.62 pp is known only from the Crossref abstract (SSRN returned 403 to curl and WebFetch; no arXiv or other copy found); the follower sample, period, copy-trade identification and cost treatment are unknown.

The Data API v2 feed streamed within 4-16 s in one ten-minute window and stalled for 3-6 minutes in three later windows on a Sunday NFL evening; whether the stalls are load-dependent, cache TTLs or steady state is unknown, but no window showed it reliable for detection.

The follower-slippage samples (two windows of 25 fills, ages 0.2-20 min) mix maker and taker rows because `/v2/trades` has no maker/taker field; a +3 s shadow book on taker fills only is still needed for a real slippage number.

The sign-randomisation nulls were run at event level on realised PnL only (open positions and merges excluded) and only for wallets with complete closed-position ledgers (Theo4, Fredi9999); high-frequency wallets returned incomplete pages and HTTP 429.

No audited follower-realised PnL exists anywhere; the expected-results range is a guess bounded by three self-reported accounts, and the +$171 paper result's filter is unproven by its own author's counterfactual.
The CLOB market WebSocket's latency was not measured (no client in the session); on-chain 2 s detection rests on block time plus the RPC, not on a measured copier.
`/v2/user-stats` realised and unrealised PnL for e46m3 moved by ~$70k between reads 50 minutes apart; wallet-level figures are snapshots.
